correctness.rationale: For every j, generic section j-faces biject to cut simplex (j+1)-faces, and integrating the admissible offset interval gives the exact sum of projection lengths. Haar-normal Gaussian radial independence turns these into Gaussian expected ranges with exactly the same normalizing factor. Rank probabilities are normalized Gaussian expected adjacent spacings, and a telescoping endpoint identity plus normal quantile estimates proves the 1−U² limit; uniform L² bounds justify expectation limits. Uniformly for fixed j and 1≪M_n≪n, the exact binomial face formula yields f_j∼M_n n^{j+1}/(j+1)!. Standalone finite checker passed full low-dimensional combinatorial tests, Gaussian integral identities, and sampled Crofton means; limits rely on proof, not experiments.

value.rationale: The exact distribution and all face-count expectations for Crofton-random affine sections give a natural complete stochastic classification of regular-simplex hyperplane cuts. The high-dimensional logarithmic law shows a genuinely nonconcentrating, continuously random polynomial complexity exponent j+2−U², sharply unlike the known fixed-centroid chi-square law and the nearly quadratic mean; this identifies a meaningful difference between random affine and central slicing rather than a routine coefficient adjustment.
